title: Conjecture 7
statement_text: (a) The diagonal online random Ramsey numbers satisfy $$\tilde{r}_{rand}(n, n) = 2^{(1+o(1)) \frac{2}{3} n}.$$ (b) The off-diagonal online random Ramsey numbers ($m \geq 3$ fixed and $n \to \infty$) satisfy $$\tilde{r}_{rand}(m, n) = n^{(1+o(1)) \frac{2}{3} m}.$$
context_text: In the $(m,n)$-online Ramsey game, played on an infinite set of initially isolated vertices, Builder adds one edge per turn and Painter immediately colours it red or blue; the online Ramsey number $\tilde r(m,n)$ is the minimum number of turns Builder needs to guarantee a red $K_m$ or a blue $K_n$. One has $\frac12r(m,n)\le\tilde r(m,n)\le\binom{r(m,n)}{2}$. $\tilde r(m,n;p)$ is the number of turns Builder needs to win with probability at least $1/2$ against a Painter who colours each edge red independently with probability $p$, and the online random Ramsey number is $\tilde r_{rand}(m,n)=\max_{p\in(0,1)}\tilde r(m,n;p)$. In the Subgraph Query Game on the random graph $G(\mathbb{Z},p)$, Builder queries one pair of vertices per step and learns whether it is an edge (each edge present independently with probability $p$, each pair queried at most once), and $f(H,p)$ is the minimum number of queries needed to find a copy of $H$ with probability at least $1/2$. The two games are related: $\tilde r(m,n;p)\le\min\{f(K_m,p),f(K_n,1-p)\}\le3\tilde r(m,n;p)$. The authors conjecture $f(K_m,p)=2^{o(m)}p^{-\frac23m+c_m}$ for $m\ge4$ with an explicit $c_m$, prove the upper bound and the cases $m=4,5$, and show that this conjecture implies both parts of the present one. Using a random Painter they prove $\tilde r(n,n)\ge2^{(2-\sqrt2)n-O(1)}$ and, for fixed $m\ge3$, $\tilde r(m,n)\ge n^{(2-\sqrt2)m-O(1)}$.
paper_title: Online Ramsey Numbers and the Subgraph Query Problem

title: Conjecture 9
statement_text: For any $m\ge4$, $f(K_m,p)=2^{o(m)}p^{-\frac{2}{3}m+c_m}$, where $c_m=\frac{m}{2m-3}$ if $m\equiv0\pmod 3$, $c_m=\frac{2}{3}$ if $m\equiv1\pmod 3$, and $c_m=\frac{2m+8}{6m-3}$ if $m\equiv2\pmod 3$.
context_text: In the Subgraph Query Game on the random graph $G(\mathbb{Z},p)$, Builder queries one pair of vertices per step and learns whether it is an edge (each edge present independently with probability $p$, each pair queried at most once), and $f(H,p)$ is the minimum number of queries needed to find a copy of $H$ with probability at least $1/2$. (The variant counting expected copies is avoided because some strategies have tiny success probability but huge expectation.) The authors prove the upper bound of the conjecture by an explicit strategy. They also show that if $H$ contains $k$ vertex-disjoint edges then $f(H,p)=\Omega_H(p^{-(e(H)-k(k-1))/(v(H)-k)})$, which gives $f(K_3,p)=\Theta(p^{-3/2})$, $f(K_4,p)=\Theta(p^{-2})$ and $f(K_5,p)=\Theta(p^{-8/3})$, proving the conjecture for $m=4,5$. For $m=6$ they only know $\Omega(p^{-13/4})\le f(K_6,p)\le O(p^{-10/3})$ and believe the upper bound is correct. The conjecture is motivated by, and would imply, the conjectured growth rates $2^{(1+o(1))\frac23n}$ and $n^{(1+o(1))\frac23m}$ of online random Ramsey numbers, through the inequality $\tilde r(m,n;p)\le\min\{f(K_m,p),f(K_n,1-p)\}\le3\tilde r(m,n;p)$, where $\tilde r(m,n;p)$ is the number of turns Builder needs to force a red $K_m$ or a blue $K_n$ with probability $1/2$ in the online Ramsey game against a Painter colouring each edge red with probability $p$.

title: Informal conjecture on generalization of Theorem 4 to all $\tilde{r}(m,n)$
statement_text: The authors prove $\tilde r(3,n)=\Omega(n^3/\log^2n)$ by a Painter strategy close in spirit to Erdős's alteration proof of the lower bound on the Ramsey number $r(3,n)$. This alteration method for lower bounding $r(3,n)$ was later generalized to all $r(m,n)$ by Krivelevich, and we suspect that the bound $\tilde r(3,n)=\Omega(n^3/\log^2n)$ can be generalized to $\tilde r(m,n)$ in the same way.
context_text: In the $(m,n)$-online Ramsey game, played on an infinite set of initially isolated vertices, Builder adds one edge per turn and Painter immediately colours it red or blue; the online Ramsey number $\tilde r(m,n)$ is the minimum number of turns Builder needs to guarantee a red $K_m$ or a blue $K_n$. One has $\frac12r(m,n)\le\tilde r(m,n)\le\binom{r(m,n)}{2}$. The Painter strategy paints every edge blue while one of its endpoints has low degree (less than $(n-1)/4$), paints an edge blue whenever red would complete a red triangle, and otherwise paints randomly. The resulting bound is $n$ times the bound on $r(3,n)$ given by the Lovász Local Lemma. With the upper bound $\tilde r(m,n)=O_m(n^m/(\log n)^{\lfloor m/2\rfloor-1})$ proved in the paper, this determines $\tilde r(3,n)$ up to a polylogarithmic factor. For general fixed $m$ the best known lower bound is $\tilde r(m,n)\ge n^{(2-\sqrt2)m-O(1)}$, from a purely random Painter. No explicit target bound for general $m$ is stated in the paper. The authors also conjecture that the triangle-free process would improve the $m=3$ lower bound to $cn^3/\log n$.
notes: No explicit quantitative bound for general $m$ is stated; only the suspicion of generalizability is expressed.
paper_title: Online Ramsey Numbers and the Subgraph Query Problem
